confirm_from.description: The same path as `from`, repeated to confirm the move.

confirm_to.description: The same path as `to`, repeated to confirm the move.

expected_hash.description: The file's hash from your last read; the move is refused if it changed since. Omit to move whatever is there now.

from.description: Vault-relative path of the file to move, including the extension, such as `attachments/photo.png`.

to.description: Vault-relative path to move it to, including the extension.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: move_file
title: Move File

description: Suggest notes that a note could link to, ranked by how many other notes link to both, each with its reasons. Use it when filling in a note's connections; search with `related_to` matches on content instead.

file.description: Vault-relative path of the note to suggest links for, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

limit.description: Most suggestions to return. Default 5, maximum 100.

offset.description: How many top suggestions to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: suggest_links
title: Suggest Links

description: A guide to Obsidian Flavored Markdown as TurboVault reads it. `quick_ref` (default): a one-page cheat sheet of wikilinks, formatting, tasks, callouts, tables, embeds, frontmatter and block references; read it before writing notes. `syntax`: the full guide, long. `example`: a note using every feature, to copy patterns from. The same texts are the resources obsidian://syntax/quick-ref, obsidian://syntax/complete-guide and obsidian://examples/sample-note.

oneOf.description: A one-page cheat sheet.
The full guide.
An example note using every feature.

name: get_ofm_guide
title: OFM Guide

description: Diff a note against another note (`right`), or against how it was before an operation in the audit trail (`operation_id`, from audit_log): a unified diff, line and word changes, and a similarity score. Give exactly one of the two. Versions aren't available on Git-backed vaults, whose history is in Git. compare_notes gives a similarity verdict without the diff.

left.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `drafts/Plan.md`.

operation_id.description: The `id` of an audit_log entry that changed `left`: diff its current content against how it was before that operation. Give this or right.

right.description: Vault-relative path of the note to diff against. Give this or operation_id.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: diff_notes
title: Diff Notes

description: Score note quality from 0 to 100 on readability, structure, completeness and staleness, with a weighted overall score and suggestions. With `path`, one note. Without it, every note: the average and distribution, per-dimension averages, the lowest- and highest-scoring notes and recommendations; slow on a large vault.

bottom_n.description: For the whole vault: how many of the lowest- and highest-scoring notes to list. Default 10, maximum 500.

path.description: Vault-relative path of one note to score, such as `projects/Plan.md`. Omit to score the whole vault.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: note_quality
title: Note Quality

description: Extract what a judge needs to check notes for hallucination, contradiction or redundancy. With `path`: that note's factual claims, its declared citations (a `# Citations` section), structural signals (Schema and Examples sections) and an `uncited` flag. Without it: the notes that make claims but cite nothing, most claims first, paged. TurboVault doesn't score grounding itself.

limit.description: Without `path`: most notes to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: Without `path`: how many notes to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

path.description: Vault-relative path of one note to analyze, such as `concepts/Revenue.md`. Omit to list the vault's ungrounded notes.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: analyze_grounding
title: Analyze Grounding

description: Validate the vault as an Open Knowledge Format (OKF) bundle: checks every note for OKF v0.1 conformance (parseable frontmatter with a non-empty `type`) and surfaces each concept's OKF metadata (type, title, description, resource, timestamp, citation count) plus the bundle's type vocabulary. Reports non-conformant files for use as a CI gate

subtree.description: Vault-relative folder to check, such as `concepts/`. Omit to check the whole vault.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: okf_validate
title: Validate OKF Bundle

description: Write or refresh OKF index.md files: each indexed folder gets an index.md listing its notes (with their frontmatter descriptions) and subfolders, so a reader can navigate one level at a time. Replaces an existing index.md; an index that would not change is left alone.

commit_message.description: Commit message for every index written, on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise each index gets a derived message.

directory.description: Vault-relative folder to index, such as `concepts/`. Omit for the vault root.

dry_run.description: Report the indexes that would be written without writing them. Default false.

recursive.description: Also index every folder below it. Default false.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: generate_index
title: Generate OKF Index

description: Add an entry to a folder's OKF log.md history (OKF spec section 7), under a `## YYYY-MM-DD` heading with the newest date first: a new date becomes the top section, an existing date gains another bullet. Creates log.md if there isn't one.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the log path.

date.description: The entry's date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Default today, in local time.

directory.description: Vault-relative folder whose log.md to append to, such as `concepts/`. Omit for the vault root.

kind.description: The entry's leading bold word, such as `Update`, `Creation` or `Deprecation`. Default `Update`.

text.description: The entry's text, one line of prose.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: append_log_entry
title: Append OKF Log Entry

description: Write the vault's link graph as one self-contained HTML page into the vault: an interactive graph of every note, a panel showing each note's rendered text and backlinks, and filtering and search. It opens in any browser with no server; the graph and markdown libraries load from a CDN.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the output path.

name.description: Title shown in the page. Default the vault folder's name.

output.description: Vault-relative path to write the HTML to. Default `viz.html`; an existing file there is replaced.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: visualize
title: Visualize Vault

description: List notes not modified for a number of days, least recently modified first, with their age. Use it to find notes due for review.

limit.description: Most notes to return. Default 20, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many of the stalest notes to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000.

threshold_days.description: Only notes not modified for at least this many days count as stale. Default 90.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: find_stale_notes
title: Find Stale Notes

description: Find notes by meaning rather than exact words, ranked by TF-IDF cosine similarity: notes about a topic (`query`), or notes most like a given note (`path`). Give exactly one. Use search for exact keywords and phrases, and find_duplicates to scan the vault for near copies.

limit.description: Most notes to return. Default 10, maximum 100.

offset.description: How many top results to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000.

path.description: Vault-relative path of a note to find look-alikes of, such as `projects/Plan.md`. Give this or query.

query.description: What to look for, in plain words, such as `quarterly revenue forecast`. Give this or path.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: find_similar
title: Find Similar

description: Scan the whole vault for pairs of notes with nearly the same content, each with its similarity score, most similar first. Slow on a large vault; compare_notes checks one pair.

limit.description: Stop after finding this many pairs. Default 20, maximum 500. The scan ends early, so it can't be paged; raise the limit to see more.

threshold.description: Lowest similarity, from 0.0 to 1.0, for a pair to count as duplicates. Default 0.8.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: find_duplicates
title: Find Duplicates

description: Compare two notes: how alike their content is (a similarity score, the terms they share, a short diff summary and a recommendation such as merging them) and how strongly the link graph connects them (`link_strength`, 0.0 to 1.0, from links in each direction and notes linking to both). diff_notes gives the full line-by-line diff.

left.description: Vault-relative path of the first note, including the extension, such as `drafts/Plan.md`.

right.description: Vault-relative path of the second note, including the extension.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: compare_notes
title: Compare Notes

description: Check notes for problems Obsidian would trip on: frontmatter that doesn't parse, `tags`, `aliases` and `cssclasses` written the pre-1.9 way (a string, or the singular keys, which Obsidian 1.9 and later ignore), broken links and malformed content. Each issue has its severity, note, line and a suggested fix. With `path`, one note; without it, the whole vault. Run it after upgrading from an older Obsidian.

IssueSeverity.description: How serious a validation issue is, least to most.

limit.description: Most issues to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

min_severity.description: Only list issues at least this serious: `info` (default, everything), `warning`, `error` or `critical`. The counts always cover every issue.

offset.description: How many issues to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

path.description: Vault-relative path of one note to check, such as `projects/Plan.md`. Omit to check the whole vault.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: validate_vault
title: Validate Vault

description: List the changes TurboVault made to the vault, newest first: each operation's id, type, path, time and content hashes. Use an id with diff_notes (operation_id), rollback_preview or rollback_note. With `summary: true`, return the trail's statistics instead: operations of each type, snapshot storage used, the time span covered and whether the entries' hash chain is intact. Not available on Git-backed vaults, whose history is in Git.

limit.description: Most entries to return. Default 50, maximum 1000.

offset.description: How many of the newest matching entries to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

operation.description: Only operations of this type: `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MOVE` or `ROLLBACK`.

path.description: Only operations on paths containing this text, such as `projects/` or `Plan.md`.

summary.description: Return the trail's statistics instead of its entries. Default false; the filters and paging don't apply to it.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: audit_log
title: Audit Log

description: Show what rollback_note would do for an operation, without doing it: the diff between the note now and the content it would be restored to, and any warnings. Not available on Git-backed vaults.

operation_id.description: The `id` of the audit_log entry to undo.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: rollback_preview
title: Preview Rollback

description: Undo one operation from the audit trail: restore the note to its content before it, or remove a note it created. Refuses if the note changed since that operation, since the later change would be lost; check rollback_preview, then pass force to roll back anyway (a client that supports elicitation asks the user to confirm). A rollback is itself recorded, so it can be rolled back. Not available on Git-backed vaults.

force.description: Roll back even though the note changed since that operation, discarding the later change. Default false.

operation_id.description: The `id` of the audit_log entry to undo.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: rollback_note
title: Roll Back Note

description: Read an Obsidian canvas (.canvas, JSON Canvas 1.0): its nodes (text, file, link, group), edges, and the notes it points at. A read that returns every node also returns the `hash` write_canvas takes as expected_hash. Large canvases come back a page of nodes at a time.

limit.description: Most nodes to return. Default 200, maximum 1000.

offset.description: How many nodes to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the canvas, ending in .canvas, such as `boards/Plan.canvas`.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: read_canvas
title: Read Canvas

description: Create or replace an Obsidian canvas (.canvas) with a whole JSON Canvas 1.0 document, validated first: unique ids, the fields each node type needs, integer positions and sizes, edges between existing nodes. Replacing an existing canvas needs the expected_hash from a read_canvas that returned every node. Written the way Obsidian writes canvases.

canvas.description: The whole canvas: `{"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}`. A node has id, type (text, file, link or group), integer x, y, width and height, optional color ("1" to "6" or a hex color), and text (text nodes), file and optional subpath starting with # (file nodes), url (link nodes) or optional label, background and backgroundStyle (groups). An edge has id, fromNode, toNode, and optional fromSide/toSide (top, right, bottom, left), fromEnd/toEnd (none, arrow), color and label.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the path.

expected_hash.description: The canvas's `hash` from a read_canvas that returned every node. Required to replace an existing canvas, and the write is refused if it changed since. `blind` replaces without checking; `absent` insists the canvas doesn't exist yet.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the canvas, ending in .canvas, such as `boards/Plan.canvas`. Missing folders are created.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: write_canvas
title: Write Canvas

description: Run an Obsidian base (.base file): its filters, formulas, sort, grouping and limit over the vault's notes, returning the chosen view's rows and columns. Evaluates the Bases expression language (note and file properties, file.hasTag, file.inFolder, file.hasLink, if, date arithmetic, string, number, list and date methods); a function it doesn't evaluate is refused by name. For ad hoc frontmatter queries without a .base file, use query_frontmatter_sql.

limit.description: Most rows to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many rows to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the base, ending in .base, such as `Reading.base`.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

view.description: The view's name. Default: the base's first view; the result lists every view's name.

name: query_base
title: Query Base

description: Find tasks (Markdown checkboxes) across the vault by status, due and scheduled dates, tag, folder, priority and text, reading Tasks plugin emoji (📅 due, ⏳ scheduled, 🛫 start, ✅ done, 🔺⏫🔼🔽⏬ priority) and Dataview fields ([due:: 2026-10-20]). Sorted by due date (undated last), then priority, then note and line. Every filter given must match.

due_after.description: Only tasks due on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD.

due_before.description: Only tasks due on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD.

limit.description: Most tasks to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many tasks to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

path.description: Only tasks in this note (vault-relative path) or folder, at any depth, such as `projects`.

priority.description: Priorities to include: highest, high, medium, normal, low, lowest. Default: all.

scheduled_after.description: Only tasks scheduled on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD.

scheduled_before.description: Only tasks scheduled on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD.

status.description: Statuses to include: todo `[ ]`, done `[x]`, in_progress `[/]`, cancelled `[-]`, other (a custom checkbox character). Default: all.

tag.description: Only tasks carrying this tag, with or without #. `work` also matches `#work/client`.

text.description: Only tasks whose description contains this text, ignoring case.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: query_tasks
title: Query Tasks

description: Find the daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly note for a date, named and placed by the vault's own Daily notes or Periodic Notes settings, and return its markdown and hash. With create, a missing note is made from the configured template, its {{date}}, {{title}} and {{time}} variables filled; an existing note is never replaced.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault when creating. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the path.

create.description: True to create the note from its template when it doesn't exist. Default false, which only reports where it would be.

date.description: A date in the period, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: today, on the server's clock.

period.description: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly.

vault.description: Name of a registered vault to run this call against (see list_vaults). Default: the active vault. Naming one doesn't change the active vault, so concurrent sessions can each work on their own.

name: get_periodic_note
title: Get Periodic Note
